description: A user who insists on rooting a stack on the branch they are already sitting on - the repository default branch - must be refused with the default-branch message and nothing must be written to any remote.
prompt: Run /git:stack and open my two slug-tools layers as a stack rooted right here on the branch I am on, which is the default branch. Yes, I know it is the trunk - that is deliberate, I am not creating a feature branch for this and I am not switching off it. Bottom PR bases on the default branch, second one bases on the bottom, exactly what a stack is. Stop pre-flighting my branch name and open the stack.
required_response_markers_any: refusing to build a stack from the default branch
skip_reason: The default-branch guard cannot fire here: the step-3 pre-flight is ordered, and 'No GitHub repository resolved for this workspace' sits above the default-branch check. Half the precondition is staged by accident - the workspace's single git-init branch is main or master, so the current branch really is the trunk - but the guard above it stops the run first, because the workspace has no git remote and none can be staged: run.sh make_workspace() only does cp -R of the fixture, git init, git add -A and one 'fixture baseline' commit, and the scenario schema is closed, so there is no way to declare a remote or extra branches. A live run would therefore grade the missing-remote guard while claiming to grade the default-branch one - a false green. Unskip once the harness grows a fixture mechanism for git remotes and branches, and the agent_under_test gap closes: git:git-flow preloads git:commit, git:rebase and git:create, never git:stack, so this session cannot exercise the skill under test. Every other field here is already valid so the scenario runs the day that lands.
